comparison: The Rust integration test compares complete serialized config models, warning order, rule sources and error strings with the read-only Python baseline after source path normalization. It separately compares load_unit_settings and checks projection into the existing S2 import, period, rule and external-engine config contracts.
preserved: Required and optional worksheet handling, header aliases, required header ordering, and general-settings defaults
Indicator code normalization, duplicate handling, missing-form warnings, and indicator flags
External-rule validation, severity compatibility mapping, enabled defaults, and source row identity
Institution lookup maps, alias columns, disabled-row filtering, and report-item metadata
Preferred strategy-sheet parsing, legacy period-band parsing, severity mapping, sorting, overlap/gap and description warnings
Rule IDs, default rule type/severity, unsupported-type warnings, unknown numeric references, and source references
Mapping of the loaded configuration into the existing S2 import, period, expression-rule, and external-comparison configuration models
scope: S2 runtime configuration workbook loading and shared unit-settings loading from synthetic XLSX fixtures using the shared Rust Calamine reader. The module is not connected to service orchestration or a production route.
unverified: real sanitized or production S2 configuration workbooks
configuration checker/preflight UI and write_default_config workbook generation
formula-valued configuration cells, date-typed configuration values, unusual worksheet dimensions, and style-only trailing rows
performance, peak memory, Windows, Kylin/UOS, glibc 2.28, and offline packaging
rollback: Revert s2_config, its module export, the supporting serialization/source fields on the S2 engine config models, synthetic workbook fixture generator and fixtures, Python baseline generator/output, parity test/report, migration-inventory row, and matching change record together. The original Python project remains read-only.
